name: Marktplatz and Village Core
description: The historic center around the Marktplatz square, where pastel houses, narrow lanes, churches, and the famous lakefront viewpoints cluster tightly against the water. It is the most beautiful and the most crowded part of the village, at its magical best in the early morning before the tour buses arrive.
bestFor: First-time visitors and photographers wanting to be in the heart of it
pros: Cafes, restaurants, and shops on your doorstep

name: Lahn
description: The flatter southern end of the village, home to the bus stop, the salt-mine funicular, the Konsum grocery, parking, and lake access. Less picture-perfect than the core but far more functional, Lahn is where daily logistics happen and where many services and quieter guesthouses sit.
bestFor: Visitors who value convenience and easy transport connections
pros: Bus stop and salt-mine funicular nearby
cons: Less postcard charm than the center

name: Obertraun
description: A relaxed village at the southeastern end of Lake Hallstatt, gateway to the Dachstein ice caves, the Five Fingers viewpoint, and the Krippenstein cable car. Quieter and more affordable than Hallstatt itself, it offers a peaceful base with easy train and ferry links to the famous village.
bestFor: Hikers and budget-minded travelers wanting calm and space
cons: A short trip from Hallstatt's core

name: Bad Goisern
description: A larger market town a short drive or train ride north of Hallstatt, with more everyday amenities, shops, and reasonably priced accommodation. It lacks the lakeside drama but works well as an affordable, well-connected base for exploring the wider Salzkammergut region by car or rail.
bestFor: Longer stays and travelers prioritizing value and amenities
cons: Not on the famous Hallstatt lakefront
Requires transport to reach the village
